title: The meek (Matthew 5:5)
hookLine: meek means strength held gently, not weakness

lines: NOBODY PUTS MEEK ON A RESUME.
cards: Nobody puts meek on a resume. It sounds like the kid who gets his lunch money taken: mousy, timid, a pushover. Meek and mild.

In most offices, the meek don't inherit anything; they get talked over in meetings. So the third line of the sermon lands strangely. The meek are blessed, and not only that: they're going to inherit the whole earth.
Either the world has meek wrong, or the sermon does.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth." This isn't new.
It's almost word for word from Psalm 37: "But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace."
In that psalm, the meek don't fret about the wicked getting ahead, and don't grab for themselves; they wait for God. The Greek word is praus.

teach.h: PRAUS: A HORSE THAT TAKES THE BRIDLE.
teach.b: Greek writers used it for a gentle person, and for a wild animal tamed: a horse that has learned to take the bridle. A tamed horse isn't weak.
It's every bit as strong as before; its strength is just under control, not thrashing around. That's meek: strength, held gently. Look who the Bible calls meek.
Moses, of all people: the book of Numbers says he was very meek, above all the men on the face of the earth. The man who stood up to Pharaoh.
And Jesus says of himself, I am meek and lowly in heart: the same Jesus who turned over tables in the temple. So meek can't mean spineless.
It's someone who could hit back and doesn't; who could take and doesn't; who doesn't need to win every argument to know who they are.
And the promise: they shall inherit the earth.
Inherit is a gift word. You don't seize an inheritance; it's given to you. The grabbers take and take.

how: Christians often name meekness, or gentleness, among the virtues they pray for; Paul lists it as a fruit of the Spirit, and many Christians practice it as holding back anger and not insisting on their own way.

o: strong, but gentle and in control of that strength
angry inside but too scared to say so
quiet and shy, easily pushed around by others

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: the meek shall inherit the earth

s: meek in the Bible means weak or timid
praus was used of strength under control, like a tamed horse.
blessed are the meek quotes a psalm
Psalm 37: the meek shall inherit the earth.
Numbers 12:3: very meek, above all the men on the face of the earth.

games.q: someone at work takes credit for your idea in front of everyone. you could humiliate them right now. what does meek look like?
o: say nothing, ever, and let it go on.
hold your strength, and speak plainly and gently later.
games.why: meek isn't weak: it's strength under control. Moses was called very meek, and he still stood before Pharaoh.

practice: Think of the person who most easily gets under your skin, and picture the moment they say the thing that sets you off; feel the sharp reply already loaded, and its strength.
Now hold it, the way a rider holds the reins: not swallowing it forever, just not letting it bolt. If you pray, you can ask for gentleness.

wordCard.voice: Meek. Praus in Greek: not weak, but gentle strength, like a strong horse that takes the bridle.

orig.note: Greek: the meek, the gentle. Matthew 5:5. the singular is praus.

carryVoice: Your line: strength, held gently. Meek was never the same as weak. That's day two hundred thirty-five.
